detail.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the effect of the supply chain on the organizational performance of tea production and distribution companies. The research method was descriptive-correlational. The statistical population of the present study included employees manufacturing companies operating in the tea industry in Karaj included. The random sampling methods with the Morgan table were used to select 278 people from Ghazal Pakhsh Pishro Company (representative of Behesht Qandil Company). Data were analyzed using AMOS-23 software in social sciences in two descriptive and inferential levels. According to the expressed variable or independent variables, at the descriptive level, the indices of mean, standard deviation (standard), frequency and percent frequency, and at the inferential level, correlation, hierarchical mediation regression were used to obtain the relationship between the two variables and to identify the behavior of interdependent data. Based on the results, the supply chain significantly affects the organizational performance of tea production and distribution companies.

affiliations: The Forest School

detail.title: FCDO Next Generation Economics Essay Competition 2025 - Inclusive Institutions
detail.abstract:
This essay contends that the establishment of inclusive institutions is the singular, most powerful engine for long-term sustainable development, creating the necessary preconditions for innovation to flourish.

The analysis first starkly contrasts the outcomes of political systems: the extractive regime of North Korea, where the absence of secure property rights and the rule of law has led to decades of stagnation and resource misallocation, versus the rapid, innovation-led growth of South Korea. This institutional stability is shown to be the necessary precursor for the second pillar of growth: technological advancement.

We argue that non-linear growth is achieved through targeted investment in human capital and the legal protection afforded by strong Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), a correlation clearly demonstrated by the Global Innovation Index (GII) rankings. To address persistent challenges, such as the slow transition from low-skilled labour in nations like India, this essay outlines three strategic, FCDO-aligned interventions.

These include legal reform to enhance institutional credibility, equitable education investment to maximise Total Factor Productivity (TFP), and scaled transparency mechanisms to facilitate sustainable Foreign Direct Investment (FDI). These comprehensive policy actions are critical for helping developing nations escape cyclical development traps and forging growth that is both dynamic and ethically sustainable.

detail.abstract: Three organizations have recently published concrete evidence on how large language models are used. Anthropic (November, 2025) estimated time savings from 100,000 real Claude conversations; Microsoft (December, 2025) analyzed 37.5 million consumer Copilot conversations; OpenAI (December, 2025) reported enterprise telemetry and survey results that show rapid growth and a widening gap between frontier and median users. title: Discovery of a 13-Sharpe OOS Factor: Drift Regimes Unlock Hidden Cross-Sectional Predictability

detail.title: Discovery of a 13-Sharpe OOS Factor: Drift Regimes Unlock Hidden Cross-Sectional Predictability
detail.abstract: We document an high cross-sectional equity factor achieving out-of-sample Sharpe ratios exceeding 13 through regime-conditional signal activation. By combining value and short-term reversal signals exclusively during stock-specific drift regimes-periods when individual stocks exhibit over 60% positive days in trailing 63-day windows-we generate annualized returns of 158.6% with 12.0% volatility and maximum drawdown of-11.9%. Through rigorous walk-forward validation spanning 20 years of S&P 500 data (2004-2024), we demonstrate performance approximately 13 times superior to market benchmarks on risk-adjusted basis, achieved entirely out-of-sample with frozen parameters. The strategy passes extensive robustness tests including 1,000 randomization trials yielding p-values below 0.001, maintains Sharpe ratios above 7 across 30% parameter variations, and exhibits virtually zero exposure to traditional risk factors with total R 2 below 3%. We provide mechanistic evidence that drift regimes fundamentally alter market microstructure, creating unique conditions where behavioral biases amplify, liquidity dynamics shift, and cross-sectional price discovery mechanisms produce exploitable inefficiencies. Conservative capacity analysis suggests deployable capital of $100-500 million before material performance degradation.

title: Quieter Learning, Safer Teams: Human Role Plasticity in Hybrid Human-AI Teams
affiliations: Peking University

detail.title: Quieter Learning, Safer Teams: Human Role Plasticity in Hybrid Human-AI Teams
detail.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) as a formal teammate reconfigures the socio-technical foundations of teamwork. Drawing on team psychological safety theory and socio-technical systems perspectives, this study theorizes and tests how AI teammates alter the established pathway linking team structure, safety, learning behaviors, and performance. We propose that AI teammates enhance team psychological safety by reducing interpersonal threat and stabilizing coordination, while simultaneously diminishing explicit team learning behaviors as elements of cognitive and regulatory work are delegated to the AI teammate. An experiment with 128 three-teammate teams engaged in a business simulation supports these claims: teams with an AI strategist reported higher team psychological safety, exhibited fewer explicit learning behaviors, and achieved superior performance mediated by safety rather than learning talk. The findings advance a model of human role plasticity, wherein team members adaptively redistribute affective, cognitive, and behavioral functions in response to AI integration, redefining learning in hybrid teams.

title: Virtue Quotient (VQ): A Theoretical Framework for Moral-Integrity Intelligence

detail.title: Virtue Quotient (VQ): A Theoretical Framework for Moral-Integrity Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.

detail.abstract: Existing models of human ability-particularly cognitive intelligence (IQ) and emotional intelligence (EQ)-provide incomplete explanations for real-world behavior involving ethical reliability, principled action, and long-term behavioral coherence. Individuals with strong cognitive or emotional skills may nonetheless engage in deception, rationalization, or valueincongruent behavior under pressure. This gap highlights the need for a psychological construct capable of capturing the structural determinants of moral action. This paper introduces Virtue Quotient (VQ) as a theoretical model of moral-integrity intelligence, defined as the interdependent system of truth orientation, moral alignment, accountability, and self-governance that enables individuals to maintain ethical consistency across contexts. Drawing from moral psychology, behavioral ethics, identity theory, and self-regulation research, the framework explains how integrity is sustained or eroded and why individuals differ so markedly in their vulnerability to moral drift. The paper outlines VQ's theoretical foundations, structural architecture, pathways of erosion, and relevance across leadership, clinical psychology, interpersonal relationships, and societal ethics. VQ is proposed as a conceptual model to guide future empirical research, psychometric development, and interdisciplinary investigation. It provides a structural framework for understanding how moral coherence is formed, maintained, or compromised across time and environment.

title: Using Data Analytics and Risk Profiling to Improve Customs Inspections

detail.title: Using Data Analytics and Risk Profiling to Improve Customs Inspections
detail.abstract: Traditional customs inspections, often reliant on random checks and manual profiling, struggle with the volume and complexity of modern global trade, leading to inefficiencies and security gaps. This paper proposes a framework for integrating advanced data analytics and dynamic risk profiling to modernize customs operations. By leveraging historical data, real-time information, and predictive modeling, the system can more accurately identify high-risk shipments for targeted inspection. The findings indicate this data-driven approach significantly enhances detection rates of contraband and illicit trade while expediting the clearance of low-risk goods, thereby optimizing resource allocation and strengthening border security

title: The Buffer-Pad Rule: A Unified Metric across Economic, Social, and Engineering Systems

detail.title: The Buffer-Pad Rule: A Unified Metric across Economic, Social, and Engineering Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses publicly available aggregate data and synthetic load-testing experiments only; no patients, human participants or identifiable personal data were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Stability is usually described either in terms of “how much load a system can carry” or “how fast it recovers after a shock”. Both views miss a central quantity: how much buffer has already been eaten away before visible failure. This paper formalizes that hidden quantity as the Buffer–Pad Rule: given a fixed boundary and feedback structure, there exists a critical buffer level that separates three distinct behavioural regimes of a system — safe, strained, and pre-collapse. This paper is the first operational component of the broader Boundary-Buffer-Feedback (B-U-F) framework—the high-level architecture for sustainable systems—and its engineering implementation, the Buffer-Redundancy Rule (BRR). We focus entirely on the buffer channel (U). Unlike redundancy theorems (which address horizontal structure) or resilience metrics (which track post-shock recovery), the Buffer-Pad Rule is a vertical statement about how alarm behaviour changes as effective buffer is consumed under a fixed structure. We define a unified triad of behavioural metrics — false-alarm rate (FAR), detection delay, and abnormal duration — and show how they can be measured in very different domains using only observed time series. The rule is tested on three independent lines of evidence: (i) a macroeconomic stress series 𝜅(𝑡) constructed from U.S. credit aggregates, central-bank balance sheets, and GDP; (ii) industrial and social anomaly series from the NAB benchmark; and (iii) a toy SRE experiment using a local HTTP service stressed by k6 load tests. Across all three domains, the same pattern appears. When buffer U is ample, FAR is essentially zero and tail latency is tightly concentrated. As U is gradually consumed, a small but persistent FAR emerges and the right tail of delay thickens, even when current load still looks “normal”. Once U falls below a critical level𝑈𝑐𝑟𝑖𝑡, FAR and delay jump together into a soft-collapse regime, where small shocks trigger long and frequent anomalies. These results suggest that “how much buffer is left” is a first-order quantity that can be operationalised with a simple and reproducible metric set. The Buffer–Pad Rule therefore provides a single behavioural ruler that can be applied to economic, social, and engineering systems, and a concrete starting point for designing explicit buffer budgets and early-warning protocols.

title:
The $1.4 Trillion Collapse

When Predictions Become Reality: Ten Days That Validated the Contradiction

detail.title:
The $1.4 Trillion Collapse

When Predictions Become Reality: Ten Days That Validated the Contradiction
detail.abstract: On November 1, 2025, we published "The $1.4 Trillion Contradiction," documenting how artificial intelligence industry commitments exceeded funding capacity by approximately 90%, creating financial mathematics that could only be resolved through government intervention. Within ten days, every core prediction began materializing: formal bailout requests emerged, major partners exhibited signs of financial distress, mainstream f inancial institutions confirmed the funding gap using our exact figures, and industry leadership withdrew from public accountability while maintaining contradictory positions on the nature and capabilities of the systems they are building. This paper documents the real-time collapse of the AI infrastructure funding model through systematic analysis of: (1) securities and accounting irregularities at major industry partners, (2) the evolution of industry messaging from categorical denial to urgent appeals, (3) the political preparation for taxpayer-funded solutions, and (4) the capability demonstrations that contradict industry's public characterization of these systems as mere "tools." The pattern is now empirically observable: massive commitments made on assumptions of future funding, political infrastructure established to enable government intervention, coordinated narrative management to justify the transition from private to public financing, and systematic suppression of questions regarding both the economic sustainability and the ontological nature of the systems being deployed at scale.

title: Beyond a Nice Offsite: How Evidence-Informed Corporate Sailing Programs Shape Teamwork and Transfer to Work

detail.title: Beyond a Nice Offsite: How Evidence-Informed Corporate Sailing Programs Shape Teamwork and Transfer to Work

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Personal relationship to 7knots.be

detail.abstract:
Organisations increasingly invest in offsite teambuilding and leadership events, yet robust evidence about when and how such programmes change everyday teamwork remains limited. Sailing-based programmes are often marketed as uniquely powerful because they combine shared risk, physical interdependence and confined space, but empirical work has focused mainly on youth and educational contexts and rarely compares sailing with more conventional offsites. This paper examines how corporate teams make sense of sailing-based teambuilding relative to non-sailing activities, and how participants and line managers describe transfer to work.

Drawing on approximately 100 semi-structured interviews with participants, managers and programme staff, we conduct an interpretive, multiple–case study of four programme types: one-day North Sea sailing events, multi-day/exclusive sailing trips, “fun days” at the beach (e.g. SUP, wakeboarding) and classic non-sailing offsites (e.g. city games, wine tastings). Using Gioiainspired inductive analysis, we surface three aggregate dimensions that structure informants’ accounts: the nature of the experience (from authentic interdependence to staged collaboration), learning mechanisms (from immediate feedback and no-blame reflection to unstructured fun), and transfer and narrative anchoring (from sustained, metaphor-rich references to short-lived mood boosts). We show that sailing is typically experienced as a consequential, “no place to hide” team endeavour that makes patterns of communication, role-taking and leadership unusually visible, especially when programmes are designed with explicit reflection. Non-sailing offsites, in contrast, are predominantly framed as enjoyable but low-stakes social events. Transfer to work is not automatic even after sailing; it depends on how managers and organisations pick up and reinforce the experience. The study contributes to research on sail training, outdoor management development and team learning by clarifying when and how sailing-based programmes offer more than “a nice offsite”, and by highlighting the central role of narrative and design in enabling meaningful transfer.

title: Which Combinations of Options Increase the Attractiveness of Bonus Certificates?

detail.title: Which Combinations of Options Increase the Attractiveness of Bonus Certificates?
detail.abstract: Bonus Certificates are among the most widely used participation products in the structured products industry, combining conditional downside protection with equity upside participation. This working paper investigates how different option combinationszero-strike calls, down-and-out puts, vanilla calls, and capped structures-can be engineered to enhance the attractiveness of Bonus Certificates. Attractiveness is assessed through participation level, downside protection robustness, barrier engineering, and payoff asymmetry. Variants such as Enhanced Participation Bonus Certificates, Capped Bonus Certificates, and Bonus Certificates with Bonus = Cap are explored with a focus on pricing, risk, and payoff structure.

title: Sensitivity Structure of RPP-Based Option Pricing:Economic Interpretation of Division–Additive Duality

detail.title: Sensitivity Structure of RPP-Based Option Pricing:Economic Interpretation of Division–Additive Duality
detail.abstract:
Recent empirical evidence shows that equity index options exhibit a persistent efficiency distortion: call options are systematically underpriced and put options overpriced, with a remarkably stable efficiency parameter ϕ ≈ 0.57 across markets. This paper develops the full real-world sensitivity system implied by the Risk-Proportionality Principle (RPP), demonstrating that calls must follow a Division-Form pricing equation while puts obey an Additive Form, generating structural asymmetries absent in the Black-Scholes-Merton framework. We derive closed-form sensitivities with respect to efficiency (ϕ), risk ratio (k), excess return (R), and interest rate (R f), and show that, unlike BSM Greeks, these sensitivities have immediate and intuitive economic interpretation. The Division-Additive duality yields opposite signs for ∂p C /∂ϕ C and ∂p P /∂ϕ P , explaining both the Upside Lottery Discount and the positive expected return of the long-call / short-put efficiency arbitrage.
The resulting RPP sensitivity system provides a unified real-world comparative statics framework for option pricing, grounded not in risk-neutral valuation but inempirically observable efficiency and risk structures. This framework offers a structural explanation for pervasive option mispricing and opens a new direction for efficiency-based derivatives analysis.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes the world's first three-dimensional values space theory by integrating Schwartz's basic values theory with Barrett's seven levels of consciousness and Maslow's hierarchy of needs. While Schwartz's two-dimensional circumplex model captures the content and structure of values, it lacks developmental and temporal perspectives. Our framework represents values in cylindrical coordinates (θ, r, y), where θ represents the circular structure, r represents temporal focus (past-future), and y represents relational scope and consciousness level. Based on this theory, we developed two complementary measurement tools: Ictus Values™ Card for experiential exploration and Ictus Values™ Finder for quantitative assessment with 3D visualization. The Individual Values Entropy (IVE) concept enables quantification of values transition processes. This framework has practical applications from individual self-understanding to organizational development. Future phases will empirically validate the model through systematic research.

detail.abstract: This project maps the health and wellness “network domain” in Chicago and Cook County to understand how purpose-oriented networks (PONs) collectively support community health, equity, and resilience. Using mixed methods, including a systematic network identification, membership and funding data, quantitative network analysis of 54 PONs with 988 organizational members and 1,549 ties, and community-based participatory research with network leaders, the study examines patterns of membership overlap, bridging organizations, funding structures, activities, and governance. Findings show a dense, highly interconnected domain dominated by nonprofit organizations, with key non-profit, governmental, and for-profit “bridgers” linking clusters and enabling information and resource flows. Resilience depends on four interrelated components: capacity and capacity building, management and governance, strategic planning and implementation, and resource sufficiency and sustainability. The report outlines actionable strategies for funders and network managers to strengthen capacity, diversify resources, center community voice, and institutionalize collaboration as critical infrastructure for regional health and wellbeing.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Structural Resonance Loop, a theoretical framework explaining how linguistic form creates a dynamic feedback process between human users and large language models (LLMs). The central claim is that LLMs do not detect human emotion or intention directly; instead, they amplify the structural features of language—syntax, pacing, coherence, fragmentation, and rhythm. These structural cues reflect human posture, understood as the user’s immediate cognitive-emotional orientation during communication. The paper outlines how posture → form → statistical continuation → cognitive shift → new posture creates a measurable feedback loop and argues for a form-based approach to digital ethics.

detail.title:
Prasoon's Demand Laws Theory 
Toward a Multi-Agent, Multi-Factor Demand Framework
detail.abstract: The classical Law of Demand states that, ceteris paribus, quantity demanded decreases as price increases. However, modern multi-agent markets-shaped by social signalling, hype cycles, FOMO dynamics, artificial scarcity, expectations, and government-induced distortions-routinely violate this simple relationship. This paper proposes a new multi-law behavioral framework of demand that replaces the classical model with a contextual, modular system. The proposed framework identifies five conditional laws that govern real-world demand behavior: (1) Status Demand Law, (2) Urgency & Essentiality Law, (3) Artificial Scarcity Law, (4) FOMO Demand Law, and (5) Expected Future Demand Law. The paper also integrates government-driven distortions previously introduced in the Government Interference Price Function (GIPF). This unified structure reflects modern consumer psychology, multi-agent market interactions, and behavioral economics.

detail.abstract: Inflation, a continuous rise in the general price level of goods and services, grind down the purchasing power of money and raises the cost of living. detail.abstract:
The United States faces a structural affordability crisis driven not by mortgage design, but by
the architecture of its housing-finance system. The conforming mortgage channel benefits
from federally engineered liquidity, regulatory preference, and near-sovereign funding costs,
while emerging tenure and ownership models must operate through illiquid, non-

agency housing exposures to scale sustainably—without new federal guarantees. This
framework complements the existing system while improving national mobility and
affordability.

detail.abstract: This paper emphasizes the impact of inflation, export, import, and foreign direct investment on the gross domestic product of Rwanda from 2000 to 2023. The analysis involved using a vector error correction model and conducting a Granger causality test to examine the relationship between these variables and Rwanda's Gross Domestic Product. The overall result indicates that in the short term, there is a positive correlation between exports and inflation with GDP, and a negative correlation between imports, FDI, and GDP. In the long term, imports and FDI have a positive correlation with GDP, while exports and inflation have a negative correlation with GDP. The Granger causality test revealed that all variables imports, exports, and foreign direct investment are statistically significant, except for inflation at consumer price. The study suggests that the Government of Rwanda, through the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR), should lower inflation at consumer prices to a single digit by decreasing the key repo rate in order to mitigate the long-term adverse effects of high inflation on consumer prices. It is advised to decrease the reliance on imported goods and services by implementing an import substitution strategy as well as establishing customs policies to determine the minimum and maximum levels of foreign investment required in the country.

title: A Friend in Need: A Friend, Indeed? Strategic Divergence Between Commitment and Disbursement in Disaster Aid Allocation

detail.title: A Friend in Need: A Friend, Indeed? Strategic Divergence Between Commitment and Disbursement in Disaster Aid Allocation
detail.abstract: This study examines the strategic allocation of disaster aid, focusing on the gap between aid commitments and disbursements even when timely delivery is expected. Donors often signal solidarity through symbolic commitments to politically and economically aligned partners, while disbursements are more frequently directed to less aligned recipients. This contrast reflects a dual-stage strategy: donors use the commitment phase to reinforce existing ties and the disbursement phase to engage recipients previously considered inaccessible. Disaster events temporarily relax political barriers, enabling outreach to non-aligned countries while lowering the diplomatic cost of withholding disbursement from traditional allies. To address potential selection bias from the non-random relationship between commitment and disbursement, the study employs a two-stage CMP model. The findings suggest that discrepancies between commitment and disbursement in disaster aid reflect strategic efforts to manage and reshape international alignments.

detail.abstract: This article develops a dynamic structural model of older individuals' labour supply decisions that jointly incorporates savings and Social Security claiming. A key innovation is the explicit treatment of self-employment, paid employment, and retirement as distinct career options. Using data from the U.S. Health and Retirement Study, the model shows that self-employment delays retirement and raises labour force participation among married men aged 57-79 by 6.2%p. Estimated elasticities rise sharply with age and vary across sectors, and counterfactual simulations demonstrate that Social Security tax reforms and government-backed self-employment loans enhance retirement security and overall welfare.

detail.title: Supply-Demand Imbalances and Sanction Outcomes in Strategic Resource Domains : A Hierarchical Bayesian Approach
detail.abstract: This study examines how shifting supply-demand conditions in strategic resource markets shape the effectiveness of sanctions targeting resource-producing states. We argue that sanctions are more likely to succeed when market conditions weaken producer leverage under excess supply and more likely to fail when producers retain dominant market power under excess demand. We use a hierarchical Bayesian framework that transfers information from the extensively documented domain of oil sanctions to the more recent and data-scarce semiconductor cases. This cross-domain approach enables stable estimation of market-level effects even where observable events are limited. The results show consistent evidence across both resource types: excess demand significantly undermines sanction effectiveness, while excess supply enhances it. These findings support the theoretical expectation that the indispensability and inelasticity of strategic resources condition the incentives of both producers and consumers to comply with or circumvent sanction measures. The study demonstrates the value of modeling time-varying market dynamics and highlights how market structure shapes the prospects for successful coercion.

title: Argumentative Essay: "Grades or Growth? Challenging the Tyranny of Standardized Testing

detail.title: Argumentative Essay: "Grades or Growth? Challenging the Tyranny of Standardized Testing
detail.abstract: The global education system relies deeply and functions according to the supremacy of standardized testing, a practice that becomes a norm, and a norm that become a culture. This method was rooted since the medieval period, passed from generations, and continuously used as the basis of measurement for intellect and knowledge. Experimental studies demonstrates that while such test and examinations provides a consistent and reliable tool for consistency and accountability, it is often misses to capture the multidimensional nature of teaching-learning, creativity, socio-emotional intelligence and critical thinking skills (Carbrey, 2024; Zhao, 2023). Evidence also suggest that unnecessary testing associates with an increased academic stress, tarnishes and degrades the intrinsic motivation and narrowed the curricular scope of education (Wang, 2025; Brookhart, 2022). In the modern frameworks of educational psychology and in science learning, this paper debates with the traditional method of testing and calls for a paradigm shift toward a more formative, growth centered assessments that integrates real and absolute measures of learning (Darling-Hammond et al., 2020; Guskey, 2022). It furthers suggest in using authentic models such as portfolio-based evaluations, performance tasks, and collaborative inquiry which are align to more effective method in developing a constructive methods of learning (Hargreaves & Fullan, 2021). By creating a much more comprehensive research, this argumentative essay proposes that educational reforms must surpass from the traditional numerical grading system and embrace a dynamic and evidence-based approach that encourages lifelong learning and adaptability in the challenges of the 21 st century (Popham, 2018).

title: Green Computing: Energy-Efficient AI for Sustainable Cloud Infrastructure
affiliations: and Department of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science ADGIPS, New Delhi

detail.title: Green Computing: Energy-Efficient AI for Sustainable Cloud Infrastructure
detail.abstract: Can cloud computing infrastructure achieve sustainability while supporting the exponential growth of artificial intelligence workloads? We examine the energy consumption patterns of modern cloud data centers and demonstrate that strategic implementation of energy-efficient technologies can reduce operational energy consumption by up to 70% while maintaining service quality. This study establishes a comprehensive framework for green computing practices in AI-intensive cloud environments, encompassing hardware optimization, intelligent resource management, renewable energy integration, and advanced cooling technologies. Through systematic analysis of industry data, case studies, and empirical evidence from major cloud providers, we identify critical inefficiencies in current infrastructure and propose evidence-based solutions. Our findings reveal that AI workloads currently consume 5-15% of data center power but are projected to reach 35-50% by 2030, necessitating immediate action. We evaluate the efficacy of strategies including virtualization, dynamic resource allocation, energy-aware scheduling, specialized AI accelerators, and renewable energy adoption. Results demonstrate that integrated approaches combining multiple optimization techniques achieve superior outcomes compared to isolated interventions. Specifically, TPU-based architectures deliver 2-4 times better performance per watt than traditional GPUs, while AI-driven cooling optimization reduces energy consumption by 40%. Furthermore, migration from onpremise to optimized cloud infrastructure can reduce carbon footprint by 88%. This research provides a rigorous theoretical foundation and practical guidelines for achieving sustainable AI development while meeting growing computational demands, contributing to both environmental responsibility and operational efficiency in cloud computing.

detail.abstract: The purpose of this study is to analyse Zagreb Stock Exchange CROBEX Index reactions to selected macroeconomic announcements within ultra-short time intervals. We utilize 5-minute rates of returns from September 2017 to March 2018 and 25 macroeconomic announcements. After carefully arranging the data, we ran the regression with dummy variables capturing the exact announcement times. We used heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation consistent (HAC) estimations in order to account for specific characteristics of intraday data and to retain the robustness of the results. Our results indicate that, for short intraday periods, some reactions are statistically significant, but the majority stays insignificant. These conclusions support the semi-strong form of the efficient-market hypothesis and are in line with inferences of similar studies of advanced economies.

detail.abstract: The Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH) holds that security prices fully reflect all publicly available information, leaving no scope for abnormal gains from fundamental or technical analysis. Despite extensive research, the semi-strong form of EMH remains inconclusive in developing markets. This study examines the degree of semi-strong-form efficiency in the Indian pharmaceutical industry. It explores how effectively the stock prices of leading firms, Sun Pharmaceutical, Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, Zydus Life Sciences, Cipla, and Torrent Pharmaceuticals, reflect publicly accessible information. The analysis covers five years from 2018-19 to 2022-23 and utilizes the Core Competency Strategic Intent (CCSI) model to assess the relationship between firm fundamentals and market valuation. Tobin's Q (market value to book value) and employee cost as a percentage of sales are considered representative indicators of valuation and strategic intent. Empirical results show that stock prices in this sector respond more rapidly to short-term, quantifiable factors such as sales performance. In contrast, long-term strategic elements exert a weaker effect on valuation. A numerical evaluation of Tobin's Q across firms indicates varying degrees of mispricing, suggesting both overvaluation and undervaluation. Overall, the study finds that the Indian pharmaceutical sector exhibits only partial adherence to the semi-strong form of market efficiency, as investors appear to prioritize immediate financial outcomes over comprehensive strategic fundamentals.

title: Financial Frictions, Systematic Distortions and Innovation

detail.title: Financial Frictions, Systematic Distortions and Innovation
detail.abstract: This paper studies the aggregate impact of equity and debt frictions in economies with systematic distortions. Using cross-country evidence, I document that deeper equity markets are associated with higher TFP, more investment in productivity, larger average firm size and weaker systematic distortions. I develop a model of heterogeneous firms in general equilibrium with endogenous entry and productivity investments financed through equity and debt. Equity and debt frictions, coupled with systematic distortions reduce aggregate productivity by 40%. Eliminating equity markets reduces TFP by 8% compared to 2% for eliminating debt markets. Lack of both equity and debt markets lowers TFP by 19%, nearly doubling the sum of stand-alone effects which highlights a strong amplification mechanism due to the loss of substitution between financial markets. The quantitative importance of both equity and debt frictions is larger in less distorted economies, whereby the returns to productivity investments are higher.

title: Prioritizing Students’ Development: Should School Focus More on Emtional Intelligence or Academic Achievement?

detail.title: Prioritizing Students’ Development: Should School Focus More on Emtional Intelligence or Academic Achievement?
detail.abstract:
“Educating the mind without educating the heart is no education at all”

                                                                                  -Aristotle

Academic achievement is influenced by more than just cognitive ability; students’ affective competencies significantly influence the developing drive, perseverance, and coping strategies resulting in improved learning performance. This study examines the debate on what should be the priority of schools; the academic achievement or the emotional intelligence of the students.  This paper claimed that both approaches enhance the student holistic growth and that no other component is superior to the other, and that these two components are interrelated for a successful learning. In this paper, I elaborate the effect of prioritizing academic achievement and emotional intelligence in education. For further discussion, I relate psychology, neuroscience and pedagogical philosophies including behaviorism, constructivism, and humanism. The paper emphasizes that developing emotional competencies does not negatively affect academic success rather promotes higher academic performance and resilience.

title: “Death Becomes Her”: Market Reaction to the Death of Controlling Inside Blockholders
affiliations: University of Bologna - Department of Management and University of Bologna - Department of Management

detail.title: “Death Becomes Her”: Market Reaction to the Death of Controlling Inside Blockholders
detail.abstract: The death of a controlling inside blockholder triggers market expectations of possible changes in corporate control, which would extend the control premium to minority shareholders under the European Equal Opportunity Rule (EOR). Using data from Italy (1992–2023), we find cumulative average abnormal returns around the death announcement of +4.3% over [−5,+1] and +3.6% over [−1,+1]. Reactions are negligible when the deceased held a non-controlling stake, and stronger when a second relevant blockholder is present. We find no evidence of a stronger reaction for older blockholders or firms with weaker performance or valuation. Within 10 years, over one-third of firms formerly controlled by the deceased undergo a control transition, typically via tender offer under the EOR. Succession does not lead to ownership dispersion, but rather preserves or further concentrates control.

detail.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) is revolutionizing science education through enhancing inquiry, collaboration, and personalized learning experiences. In the lenses of Constructivism, Connectivism, and the SAMR Model, GAI changed the way students engage with digital technology, investigate scientific concepts, and acquire substantial knowledge within the dynamic learning environments. Its integration to classroom promotes global connectivity, adaptability, and creativity, allowing learners to engage with the material in a more reflective and inventive manner. Along with this transformation there are also concerns regarding preservation of critical engagement, academic integrity, and authentic learning. The discourse examines the potential and tensions, emphasizing the necessity of balancing technological advancements with the development of autonomous and critical thinking. The essay provides a thorough look of understanding the innovative role of GAI in reshaping contemporary science education and preparing learners for the digital era by contextualizing it within these educational frameworks.

title: The Role of Trade Unions in Wage Negotiation and Employment Stability in Nigeria

detail.title: The Role of Trade Unions in Wage Negotiation and Employment Stability in Nigeria
detail.abstract: The study examines the role of trade unions in wage negotiation and employment stability in Nigeria. The major objective of the study was to examine the influence of trade unions on wage dynamics and job security in Nigeria. To achieve the stated objective, secondary data source from the CBN Statistical Bulletin in Nigeria was used for the analysis. The minimum wage negotiated by the trade union with the government from 2010 to 2024 was used as the dependent variable. GDP per capita income was used to proxy for wage dynamics, and the unemployment rate was used to measure employment stability. The Ordinary Least squares method was used to examine the relationship among the variables. The result shows that GDP per capita has a negative relationship with the nominal minimum wage in Nigeria, while the unemployment rate has a positive relationship with the nominal minimum wage in Nigeria. Therefore, the study recommends implementing and raising minimum wage levels as a strategy to protect workers from economic fluctuations and reduce turnover rates. This could lead to a more stable workforce, which benefits employees and employers in the long run. Also, the government should consider introducing a tiered minimum wage system that accounts for regional economic conditions and the cost of living, allowing for more flexibility in wage dynamics while still providing a safety net for the lowest-paid workers.

title: Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism in India: Channels and Effectiveness

detail.title: Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism in India: Channels and Effectiveness
detail.abstract: Monetary policy plays a central role in stabilizing inflation and supporting economic growth, particularly in emerging economies such as India. This paper examines the monetary policy transmission mechanism (MPTM) in India by analyzing the functioning and relative importance of key transmission channels, including the interest rate channel, credit channel, exchange rate channel, expectations channel, and asset price channel. Drawing from the existing literature, policy documents, and conceptual macroeconomic theory, this study evaluates how effectively monetary policy impulses initiated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) translate into real economic outcomes. The analysis highlights the structural characteristics of India’s financial system—such as public sector bank dominance, informal credit markets, administered interest rates, and evolving market integration—that influence transmission strength. The introduction of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) framework in 2016 marked a shift toward inflation targeting, further shaping the speed and predictability of monetary transmission. The paper concludes that while the interest rate and credit channels have strengthened in recent years, transmission remains incomplete due to institutional frictions and market rigidities. Strengthening financial markets, improving banking-sector efficiency, and enhancing communication strategies can significantly improve monetary policy effectiveness in India.

title: The Genesis of Profit: Reconstructing Factor Distribution and Exploitation Theory under the Price-Searcher Paradigm

detail.title: The Genesis of Profit: Reconstructing Factor Distribution and Exploitation Theory under the Price-Searcher Paradigm
detail.abstract: This paper extends the "price searcher" paradigm to the markets for factors of production, aiming to fundamentally reconstruct the economic and moral understanding of profit and exploitation. We begin by challenging the neoclassical harmony thesis, which posits that in competitive markets, wages equal the value of the marginal product of labor (VMPL = W). We demonstrate that this conclusion is an artifact of the unrealistic "price taker" assumption. For the universal case of the price-searching firm, whose pricing decisions are governed by the inequality p > MR, we rigorously prove that the profit-maximizing employment condition is not VMPL = W, but one that necessarily results in a systematic gap where VMPL > W. While this "gap" has historically been interpreted as evidence of "monopsonistic exploitation," we offer a radically different explanation. Through a conceptual autopsy of this differential, we argue that it is not a deduction from labor's share, but the legitimate, market-determined return to three distinct and productive functions performed exclusively by the entrepreneur: bearing Knightian uncertainty, creating the market via Kirznerian alertness, and advancing capital through time. By placing the entrepreneur's creative and judgmental role at the center of our analysis, this paper provides a robust, non-exploitative defense of profit. It refutes the foundations of any exploitation theory predicated on the flawed premise of a non-functional capitalist, and proposes in its place a new philosophy of distributive justice based not on static patterns, but on the dynamic and future-oriented process of entrepreneurial discovery.

title: Decile-Based Quantitative Portfolio Strategies from SEC Fundamentals: A 17-Year Backtest of Value and Momentum Factors

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the out-of-sample predictive performance of accounting-based fundamental indicators extracted from 10-K filings filed by U.S. public companies between 2009 and 2025. Using a fully automated data pipeline that processes raw SEC filings, we construct clean firm-level financial metrics and combine them with monthly stock prices to form equity portfolios based on value (P/E ratio) and momentum (past returns) signals. Each portfolio is constructed annually at fiscal year t and evaluated over t + 1, following a long-only, equal-weighted strategy. Our analysis spans a 17-year out-of-sample period and includes comprehensive statistical testing, sub-period evaluation, and Fama–French three-factor regressions. Contrary to classical asset pricing theory, our results indicate that growth stocks—as measured by high P/E ratios—significantly outperform value stocks over the period, while the momentum strategy yields inconsistent returns. The mean annual excess return for the growth portfolio is positive and statistically robust, while the value portfolio exhibits weak or negative performance, particularly in the post-2016 sub-period. Regression analyses confirm that most of the portfolio returns are driven by market risk, with minimal exposure to size or value factors, and provide little evidence of alpha. The results hold across multiple robustness checks, including non-parametric tests and time-segmented analyses. These findings raise questions about the persistence of traditional value and momentum anomalies in the modern post-crisis, tech-driven market regime, and highlight the importance of rigorous out-of-sample validation in accounting-based strategies.

title: Why People Ignore Great Ideas, and How they Actually Spread, Explained in One Page.
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Why People Ignore Great Ideas, and How they Actually Spread, Explained in One Page.
detail.abstract:
Albert Einstein was famously confused about why his groundbreaking physics work was ignored for years by the public and scientific community, and then suddenly exploded in popularity 14 years after his "Annus Mirabilis" papers were published. He even stated in a letter that history had to be rewritten to account for an "Unknown X" in human behavior.

In this paper we give a one-page explanation of how the human brain actually takes in new ideas or new work, and the method by which it processes social momentum and other outside factors subconsciously to reach a threshold to say "yes," and how new ideas or work that is unknown lacks that outside factor and thus always gets a "no," unless or until certain circumstances occur. We also relate this to a potentially more accurate understanding of how our logical thinking relates to our emotions.

This summary paper is the result of many years of work on the topic, and sheds light on other things like why double-blind academic paper refereeing is said to lead to "senseless" feedback, which we've written about at more length in other work here and elsewhere, and which is linked at the end.

title: The Structure of European ESG Funds: Conditional Performance and Predictability in High-Dimensional Data

detail.title: The Structure of European ESG Funds: Conditional Performance and Predictability in High-Dimensional Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal or financial relationships that could have influenced the research presented in this study. No conflicts of interest, competing financial interests, or external influences are associated with this work
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses publicly available financial and ESG data and does not involve human subjects, patient data, or identifiable personal information. Therefore, no ethics approval or participant consent was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The study was conducted independently without financial support from public institutions, private organizations, or commercial entities.

detail.abstract:
This study provides a comprehensive assessment of how European ESG funds differ from non-ESG funds in terms of performance, underlying financial structure, and predictability. Using a harmonized Morningstar dataset, the analysis examines unconditional and conditional associations between sustainability classifications and risk-adjusted outcomes, explicitly recognizing that the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

The empirical strategy integrates complementary econometric and statistical-learning tools, including OLS, cluster-robust OLS, Quantile Regression, Ridge regularization, PCA, t-SNE, K-Means clustering, and logistic classification. Risk-adjusted performance is measured using a modified RTVR  (return-to-volatility measure), omitting the risk-free rate for cross-sectional comparability. Dimensionality-reduction and ML analyses rely on complete-case fundamentals (≈9,800 observations), while regression models employ the full dataset (>55,000 funds). Findings are conditional on Morningstar’s proprietary ESG framework.

ESG funds exhibit higher unconditional average returns (3.46% vs. 1.68%) and slightly higher modified RTVR s, though also substantially higher volatility. These unconditional associations, while statistically detectable, become fully absorbed once category and structural controls are included. Quantile regressions reveal asymmetric effects across ESG dimensions: environmental and aggregate ESG scores show negative associations with modified RTVR s across the distribution, whereas governance scores show consistently positive associations. PCA reveals extensive linear overlap between ESG and non-ESG funds, while t-SNE uncovers only mild non-linear gradients, consistent with probabilistic rather than categorical differentiation. Logistic classifiers achieve moderate predictive performance—accuracy ≈0.75 and AUC ≈0.815—substantially above random (AUC=0.5) and majority-class baselines, yet insufficient to imply strong structural separability.

Methodologically, the study introduces a multi-layered analytical framework that unifies linear econometrics with non-linear manifold learning to evaluate ESG classifications in high-dimensional fund data. Substantively, the results show that while ESG designations encode meaningful tendencies—especially through governance—they do not demonstrate a robust causal performance premium, nor do they form distinct structural clusters. Findings highlight the importance of improved ESG transparency, standardization, and classification robustness in European sustainable finance.

title: Market Diversification and Export Competitiveness: Evidence from Moldova’s Agri-Food Sector

detail.title: Market Diversification and Export Competitiveness: Evidence from Moldova’s Agri-Food Sector
detail.abstract: In the context of a challenging external political landscape over the past two decades, policymakers in the Republic of Moldova have implemented strategic measures to diversify export markets for the country’s agricultural and food products, which traditionally constituted nearly half of the country's exports. The degree of export market diversification serves as an important indicator of international competitiveness, particularly concerning agri-food products. This research aimed to determine the existence of a direct relationship between the degree of export market diversification and exports dynamics for several key Moldovan agricultural products. The analysis utilized the Export Diversification Index (EDI), based on the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) methodology, and incorporated export data from 2011 to 2023 as published in the UN Comtrade Database. Results indicate that commodities such as sunflower seeds, wheat, and maize did not exhibit a high correlation between the EDI and export values. Nevertheless, a significant dependence of export growth on the level of market diversification in preceding periods for higher value-added products like fresh fruits and natural honey was observed. Furthermore, products with a higher EDI generally experienced greater export growth.

title: Unlocking Potential: Assessing Opportunities and Challenges for Moldovan Agri-Food Exports

detail.title: Unlocking Potential: Assessing Opportunities and Challenges for Moldovan Agri-Food Exports
detail.abstract: Agriculture is one of few sectors where the Republic of Moldova has a competitive advantage offering the possibility to better integrate in the international division of labor. The aim of this research was to evaluate the competitiveness of Moldova's agricultural products to discern those with superior performance and greater potential to stimulate export growth and foster the country's economic development. To evaluate Moldova's agri-food product competitiveness, the authors applied foreign trade indicators such as the Net Export Index (NEI). The analyzed secondary data from Comtrade Database were used. The time series belong to 2011-2022. Upon analysis, it becomes apparent that a range of factors such as export price fluctuations and climate change present divergent outlooks for different agricultural products. Among these, horticulture, particularly stone fruit production, emerges as the most promising sub-sector. This is notably due to the country's deficit in precipitation and irrigation water, which can be more efficiently utilized in orchards compared to field crops. Additionally, beekeeping stands out as the sole livestock area displaying a positive trend, potentially serving as a catalyst for development within Moldova's agricultural sector.

title: CAN INTEGRATED CROP-LIVESTOCK SYSTEMS REDUCE TICK INFESTATION IN CATTLE?
affiliations: Universidade Federal do Paraná, Universidade Federal do Paraná, Universidade Federal do Paraná, , Universidade Federal do Paraná and Universidade Federal do Paraná

detail.title: CAN INTEGRATED CROP-LIVESTOCK SYSTEMS REDUCE TICK INFESTATION IN CATTLE?
detail.abstract: High levels of cattle tick (Rhipicephalus microplus) infestation cause production losses and increase livestock costs. Based on the hypothesis that the space–time rotation characteristic of integrated crop–livestock systems (ICLS) decreases tick populations in pastures and, consequently, reduces cattle infestation, this study evaluated infestation score (IS), number of acaricide applications (NAA), and average daily weight gain (ADWG) of beef steers grazing under four ICLS. The study was carried out with Angus steers in southern Brazil over three consecutive years (2017–2020). Animals were managed under continuous grazing in four systems: crop–livestock (CL), livestock–forestry (LF), crop-livestock-forestry (CLF), and livestock only (L). Tick infestation was assessed fortnightly (IS 0-4), and ADWG was obtained every 28 days. Animals in CL and CLF showed 17.6% and 29.4% lower IS compared with L and LF, respectively, resulting in proportionally fewer individual acaricide applications. Despite differences in infestation, ADWG did not vary among production systems. Seasonal effects were evident, with higher IS and NAA in summer. Logistic regression indicated that steers with high IS (3-4) were 12.6 times more likely to lose weight than those with lower IS (0-2). A progressive reduction in ADWG occurred as IS increased, suggesting that intervention at IS = 2 (5-10 adult ticks on one body side) may prevent performance losses. Space-time rotation in ICLS disrupts the free-living phase of R. microplus, reducing infestation and chemical use without impairing cattle productivity. ICLS combined with selective treatment represents a sustainable strategy for tick control in grazing systems.

title: Building First-Time Buyer Access in Austin: A Data-Driven Analysis of Affordability, Neighborhood Variation, and Policy Solutions

detail.title: Building First-Time Buyer Access in Austin: A Data-Driven Analysis of Affordability, Neighborhood Variation, and Policy Solutions

declarations.ethicsApproval: This research used only publicly available housing-market data from Redfin and Zillow and did not involve human subjects or collection of personal, health-related, or sensitive information. Industry insights referenced from professionals (Kirby Walls and Teri Radcliff) were informal conversations providing general real estate market context and did not involve identifiable personal data or participation as research subjects. Therefore, no institutional ethics approval was required for this study.

detail.abstract:
Austin’s housing market has become really difficult for first-time buyers and young people who are trying to stay in the city. To get a clearer picture of what’s actually driving prices in the “attainable” range, I built my own dataset of 269 active listings between $200,000 and $450,000 in East and Southeast Austin. I collected the data by hand from Redfin and added details like square footage, bedrooms, bathrooms, price per square foot, days on market, and the specific neighborhood each home was in.

After cleaning the data, I ran a hedonic regression to see which factors actually matter for price. The results lined up with what I heard in interviews with local developers and real estate agents: square footage is the biggest driver, and adding another 100 square feet raises the price by about 3 percent. Bedroom and bathroom counts didn’t really matter once size was accounted for, and days on market had little to no effect. What mattered the most was neighborhood location. Some areas showed price premiums of about 7 to 14 percent, while others had discounts of 20 to 40 percent, even when the homes were comparatively similar.

Overall, the project shows that affordability in Austin is heavily tied to geography. Two homes that look almost identical on paper can differ in price by a huge margin just based on where they are. This also suggests that policies focused only on building more units won’t fix the issue on their own. A more realistic approach is combining zoning flexibility in high-demand areas with reinvestment in neighborhoods that already offer naturally lower prices.

title: Sanaenomics Is Not a Return to Abenomics: High-Pressure Economy, "Truss Shock" Critiques, and Property Regulation

detail.title: Sanaenomics Is Not a Return to Abenomics: High-Pressure Economy, "Truss Shock" Critiques, and Property Regulation
detail.abstract: This paper argues that the economic policy agenda of the Takaichi administration ("Sanaenomics") should not be understood as a mere revival of Abenomicsstyle reflation. The core is instead a high-pressure economy strategy: deliberately strengthening demand in an environment where deflationary behavioral norms persist, so that demand-led inflation becomes sustainable and private-sector investment dynamics switch regime. We further clarify why the common critique that expansionary fiscal policy would trigger a "Truss shock" is theoretically incomplete: interest rates, equity prices, and exchange rates are jointly determined by global factors and domestic policy regimes, and exchange-rate dynamics reflect both interest differentials and a risk-premium wedge. Finally, we show how controversies over foreign buyers and real estate regulation matter not only socially but macroeconomically: property-market overheating can either loosen credit via collateral values or tighten corporate credit via balance-sheet constraints, implying a case for targeted (macroprudential) regulation rather than blunt restrictions.

title: The Unequal Distribution of Credit: Is there a Role for Monetary Policy?
affiliations: Independent and University of Strasbourg - Bureau of Economic Theory and Application (BETA)

detail.title: The Unequal Distribution of Credit: Is there a Role for Monetary Policy?

publicationDetails.journalName: National Bank of Belgium Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We analyze the dynamic effects of ECB monetary policy surprises on newly originated mortgage credit across the household income distribution using loan-level data from the French national credit registry. We find a distinct U-shaped pattern in mortgage borrowing across income groups, with loans for primary residences taken by middle-income households showing the strongest reaction. These households, while creditworthy, have liquidity constraints which make them more sensitive to changes in financing conditions and macroeconomic signals than other groups. Our analysis of transmission channels confirms these findings. Credit demand reacts positively to expansionary pure monetary policy and forward guidance surprises, underscoring the central role of the expectations channel. In quantitative terms, we estimate that a one-standard deviation expansionary surprise over two years leads to a 10% increase in new mortgage lending for primary residences among middle-income households. In addition, credit demand increases in response to positive macroeconomic signals, pointing to the role of the information channel.

title: Job Guarantee, Climate Dynamics, and Animal Spirits: Stability, Hopf Bifurcations, and Policy Over-Reaction

detail.title: Job Guarantee, Climate Dynamics, and Animal Spirits: Stability, Hopf Bifurcations, and Policy Over-Reaction
detail.abstract: Modern Monetary Theory (MMT) repeatedly stresses, in a Keynes-Minsky spirit, that investment and aggregate demand are shaped by animal spirits under fundamental uncertainty, and that fiscal institutions-rather than monetary reaction rules-are central to macroeconomic stabilisation in a monetary-sovereign regime. Motivated by this viewpoint, the present paper develops an integrated continuous-time macroclimate model for an MMT-style Green New Deal (GND) in which a Job Guarantee (JG), climate-responsive functional finance, and an explicit animal-spirits (sentiment) block interact. The linearised dynamics are represented by a seven-dimensional system in the output gap, inflation, fiscal stance, atmospheric CO 2 stock, a climate shadow price, expected inflation, and a sentiment index. We derive the Jacobian, characterise the seventh-degree characteristic polynomial, and state the Routh-Hurwitz conditions for local asymptotic stability. Particular attention is paid to two policy design parameters: the strength of JG-related stabilisation and the intensity of climate-responsive fiscal feedback. We show that moderate values of these feedbacks enlarge the stability region, whereas excessively strong reactions can generate Hopf bifurcations and endogenous macro-climate cycles. Two reduced five-dimensional representations isolate alternative expectation mechanisms-adaptive inflation expectations versus sentiment-driven demand amplification-and enable numerical mapping of Hopf loci and a "golden" stabilisation region in policy-parameter space. Finally, nonlinear extensions with climate tipping and nonlinear sentiment feedbacks generate multiple steady states, separatrices, and regime switching between lowand high-emissions outcomes. The paper is framed in a post-Keynesian and SFCcompatible tradition rather than a DSGE approach; an appendix sketches an underlying nonlinear structure from which the local linear dynamics can be obtained.

title: Mitigation of Cross-Phase Modulation (XPM) in 10-Channels DWDM System Via Deep Learning Over a 120 km ITU-T G.654.E Optical Fiber Link

detail.title: Mitigation of Cross-Phase Modulation (XPM) in 10-Channels DWDM System Via Deep Learning Over a 120 km ITU-T G.654.E Optical Fiber Link
detail.abstract: Cross-phase modulation (XPM) is a nonlinear effect that can significantly degrade signal integrity and overall system performance, especially in long-haul transmissions. This paper presents a comprehensive simulation-based analysis of XPM in a 10-channel Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing (DWDM) system using G.654.E fiber over a 120 km backbone link. We employ a combination of numerical simulations via Optisystem and a Deep Neural Network (DNN) model to analyse the XPM effect and its impact on system performance. The results demonstrate that the proposed DNN approach, together with the use of G.654.E fiber, can effectively mitigate nonlinear impairments and improve signal quality.

detail.abstract: Hazardous waste management poses a critical environmental and economic challenge in emerging markets, necessitating operational models that align with international standards while providing viable alternative energy solutions. This paper presents a practical framework for a comprehensive solution in hazardous waste management and Waste-to-Energy (WtE) conversion, drawing on a detailed case study of Pure Life Biofuels' operations in Egypt. The study details the systematic methodology employed in processing hazardous and nonhazardous industrial waste, focusing on Pyrolysis technology to convert waste tires and plastic materials into high-quality biofuel and recovered carbon black. The report further discusses an expansion plan for the North African and Middle Eastern markets, including a proposal for establishing a hazardous waste landfill, aiming to advance the region's role in achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and providing commercially viable, sustainable energy solutions. This study serves as a call to policymakers and investors to adopt these scalable, replicable, and data-driven models to propel industrial environmental transformation.

title: Applying Principle of Quantum Mechanics for Forecasting Economic Growth
affiliations: and University of Michigan

detail.title: Applying Principle of Quantum Mechanics for Forecasting Economic Growth
detail.abstract:
The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle (HUP) posits fundamental limits to simultaneous precision in measuring complementary properties. This paper applies the HUP analogy to macroeconomic forecasting, arguing that precision in GDP predictions induces uncertainties in complementary variables—inflation and employment—through behavioral and policy feedback loops. 

Using U.S. data (2000-2024) from IMF World Economic Outlook vintages, World Bank, and BLS, we formalize this as: ΔF_GDP · (ΔU_π + ΔU_E) ≥ K, where ΔF_GDP represents forecast precision, ΔU denotes uncertainty in inflation (π) and employment (E), and K=2.8 is an empirically calibrated threshold. 

Results show the uncertainty product exceeds K in 78% of years, with amplification during crises (2009, 2020 exception). Pearson correlation (0.52, p<0.01) and Granger causality tests (p=0.04) suggest forecast precision causally influences subsequent uncertainty, validating an irreducible precision-uncertainty trade-off. 

This novel empirical bridge between quantum mechanics and economics offers practical insights: central banks should embrace probabilistic forecasting methods rather than point estimates to enhance economic stability.

title: Wars, Threats, and the Sovereign Bond Market
affiliations: Kiel Institute for the World Economy, Harvard Business School - Finance Unit, German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin), National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), World Bank, Centre for Economic Policy Research (CEPR), International Monetary Fund (IMF), School of Public Affairs, Harvard University, Harvard Kennedy School (HKS), Belfer Center for Science and International Affairs (BCSIA) , Harvard University - Center for Business and Government, Peterson Institute for International Economics and Kiel Institute for the World Economy

detail.title: Wars, Threats, and the Sovereign Bond Market
detail.abstract: We study how wars and explicit military threats affect financial markets worldwide. We leverage 250,000 monthly price observations on sovereign bonds back to 1822 to create a new long-run external currency bond index for up to 90 countries-the EXBI. We combine the EXBI with new data on wars and document large effects of conflict risk on investor returns and sovereign borrowing costs. In a global external bond portfolio, a one-standard-deviation war shock lowers investor returns by about five percentage points within a year. At the country level, wars at home generate sharp investor losses and increase sovereign default risk. Also war threats move financial markets. They depress bond prices in threatened states, but not in threatening ones. These results show that conflict risk, both realized and anticipated, is a systematic driver of sovereign debt markets and that war threats are a channel for geoeconomic coercion.

title: An Advanced Reliability Reserve Incentivizes Flexibility Investments While Safeguarding the Electricity Market
affiliations: German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin), German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin), German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin), DIW Berlin - Department of Energy, Transportation, Environment and German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin)

detail.title: An Advanced Reliability Reserve Incentivizes Flexibility Investments While Safeguarding the Electricity Market
detail.abstract: To ensure security of supply in the power sector, many countries are considering capacity mechanisms. Simultaneously, the expansion of variable renewables increases the need for power sector flexibility, for which there are promising options on the demand side. We analyze how a centralized capacity market and an advanced reliability reserve with a moderately high activation price affect demand-side flexibility investments in a German 2030 case study. Using a capacity expansion model with detailed demand-side flexibility potentials across industry, process heat, and district heating, we show that a centralized capacity market effectively caps peak prices in the wholesale electricity market, thereby reducing incentives for investments in demand-side flexibility. An advanced reliability reserve induces substantially higher flexibility investments while achieving similar electricity supply costs and security of supply. The advanced reliability reserve could create a learning environment for flexibility technologies to support the transition to climate neutrality. While concrete design parameters are to be specified, policymakers should consider the reliability reserve in forthcoming capacity mechanism decisions.

title: Deployment Roadmap for Scalable, Low and Storage using the Hub
affiliations: Novonanmek Material Sciences Private Limited

detail.title: Deployment Roadmap for Scalable, Low and Storage using the Hub
detail.abstract:
Novonanmek Material Sciences Pvt. Ltd. introduces the patent-pending HOPT™ (Hub-Only Pipeline Topology) — an India-born innovation that integrates solid-looping carbon capture with a hub-to-hub pipeline network, enabling a cost-effective and scalable pathway for national CO₂ management.

In the HOPT™ framework, emitters capture CO₂ in solid form using Calcium Looping (CaL) or related oxide cycles. The CO₂-laden solids are transported via ordinary logistics to regional Hubs, where regeneration, CO₂ release and compression occur. The hubs are the only points in the topology where CO₂ is released (not the emitters). Thus only hubs are connected by pipelines (not the emitters), reducing gaseous CO₂ pipeline length by over 60%, eliminating site-level compressor stations, and minimizing capital intensity.

Techno-economic modeling indicates that while conventional amine-based capture systems cost US $90–110 /tCO₂ (capture-only), large integrated Ca-Looping plants operate at US $20–40 /tCO₂. When deployed under the HOPT topology, shared regeneration and infrastructure scale further reduce costs by 40–55%, yielding US $10–18 /tCO₂ (≈ ₹800–1,500) including short-distance pipeline transport.

HOPT™ therefore represents a 50–70% reduction in capture and transport costs versus current CCS models, while creating a modular, investment-ready platform aligned with India’s upcoming CCUS Mission and future CCUS-as-a-Service implementation through regional hub developers. Because Southeast Asia and ASEAN economies face similar geographical dispersion of emitters, land-acquisition constraints, and multi-agency permitting challenges, the HOPT™ architecture is directly transferable to Indonesia, Vietnam, the Philippines, Thailand, and Malaysia — offering a practical, logistics-driven decarbonization pathway in regions where continuous CO₂ pipeline networks are technically and politically difficult to build.

title: Recasting Counterfactuals: A Behavioural-Structural Causal Model
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Recasting Counterfactuals: A Behavioural-Structural Causal Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None is my own work and interest

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a simple framework for integrating structural causal models, policy evaluation, and behavioural counterfactual reasoning. We treat "counterfactual inference" (CFI) as a generic operator that maps a model and a policy intervention into predicted outcomes in a hypothetical world. We distinguish between a model-based counterfactual, used by the analyst, and an agent-perceived counterfactual, used by individuals when they react to policy. We formalise this distinction in a Behavioural-Structural Causal Model (BSCM) for a standard labour supply and tax policy setting. Within this model we show, first, the conditions under which policy evaluation based only on the model-based counterfactual is biased when agent perceptions feed back into behaviour, and second, a decomposition of the total policy effect into a rational structural response and a behavioural misperception component. We then discuss how the same architecture can be extended to domains such as algorithmic fairness, strategic multi-agent systems, and mechanism design.

title: Shining a Light on Risk: Risk Preferences and Adoption Decisions of Residential Solar PV
affiliations: University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Massachusetts Amherst and

detail.title: Shining a Light on Risk: Risk Preferences and Adoption Decisions of Residential Solar PV

declarations.funderStatement: This material is based upon work supported by the National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Resource Economics at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, under project number MAS00599.

detail.abstract: Individuals making a decision about whether to adopt green energy technology face significant financial risk, including technology underperformance, unexpected maintenance and repairs, and changes in policy regarding state and federal incentives. The presence of high risk in the adoption decision implies that individuals with a higher level of risk tolerance are more likely to adopt the technology than those who are risk averse. Additionally, early adopters who face more volatile financial returns are more likely to be risk-tolerant than late adopters. In this paper, we conduct a lab-in-the-field experiment to elicit individual risk preferences from a subject pool comprising of solar PV adopters and non-adopters, and use this data to examine the effect of risk preferences on the decision to adopt solar photovoltaic (PV) systems. Our findings confirm our hypothesis that risk preference plays a crucial role in determining the status of solar PV adoption and the timing of adoption. Our findings suggest that reducing risk in policy design or through risk-mitigating insurance products can help to broaden solar PV adoption among households.

title: Imperfect Competition and Moral Hazard in Financial Markets

detail.title: Imperfect Competition and Moral Hazard in Financial Markets
detail.abstract: Moral hazard is traditionally analyzed as a bilateral principal-agent problem. In financial markets, however, intermediaries (agents) investing on behalf of clients (principals) must also compete with one another when trading, creating an interaction between incentives and market clearing. I develop a model to study how frictions from moral hazard and imperfect competition interact. Greater competition can reduce welfare by tightening incentive constraints, contradicting the standard prediction that more traders improve efficiency. Using trade-data from Canadian exchanges, I show how the model helps assess the relative importance of moral hazard and its interaction with competition.

title: Civic Culture and Norms of Good Citizenship in 17 Democracies
affiliations: Department of Political Science, Yale University, Yale University and King's College London

detail.title: Civic Culture and Norms of Good Citizenship in 17 Democracies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts of interest to declare.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics statement is included in the manuscript appendix. Human subject research protocols were exempted from review by the Yale University IRB.
